messages:
jamie: Hey team — customer 'ParcelX' seeing frequent SSE disconnects from our /stream endpoint during bursts. They report ~10-15s steady chunks then server closes connection, client reconnects immediately and gets duplicate event processing. Happening on iOS + our envoy sidecar behind corp proxy.

sasha: Thanks — any logs or request IDs?

jamie: Here's one trace from their session (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-15T16:02:10Z] conn=abcd1234 write failed: errno=11 EAGAIN, queued=9872, sndbuf=65536
[2026-03-15T16:02:10Z] conn=abcd1234 attempt_write() -> wrote=0, will_abort_after=3s
[2026-03-15T16:02:12Z] conn=abcd1234 aborting connection: persistent slow consumer
[2026-03-15T16:02:12Z] stream closed, code=1006, remote=client
```

alex: EAGAIN on send() + queued high and then abort -> sounds like our backpressure threshold is being hit. Is the client doing a very small read window? Do we see many small chunks?

maria: Customer says mobile client reads very slowly when on poor cellular. Also Envoy configured with default per-connection buffers; might be extra buffering causing burst then stall.

jamie: Repro steps I used based on their setup:
1) Start local node proxy to mimic Envoy (mitm)
2) Run netem to throttle rx: `tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 120ms rate 200kbps`
3) Curl SSE with slow consumer script that reads 32 bytes every 200ms

Script snippet: ```python
import requests, time
r = requests.get('https://local/stream', stream=True)
for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=32):
    time.sleep(0.2)
    print(len(chunk))
```

Result: connection closed after ~14s with same EAGAIN abort path.

sasha: Good repro, thanks. Two quick Qs: which variant of runtime? (hosted/dedicated/private) and is there a Dedicated sidecar config?

jamie: Hosted customer on Dedicated pool with envoy sidecar managed by them. They also reported billing double-counting on reconnects because each reconnect counted as a new session with no dedupe at their app layer. They want graceful draining not abrupt aborts.

alex: From runtime POV options: (a) increase write-queue threshold and backoff policy, (b) reduce our chunk size to avoid large queued payloads, (c) surface a Retry-After or disable immediate client reconnect via X header so apps can implement jitter. Also need to check kernel sndbuf tuning and whether our async write loop treats EAGAIN as a hard fail vs queuing for eventloop.

maria: Also check Envoy config: `per_connection_buffer_limit_bytes` and `disable_chunked_encoding` flags — proxy buffering can cause spikes. If Envoy buffers the whole HTTP response before forwarding chunks, client reading slow shouldn't cause upstream to backlog immediately, but when buffer fills it will.

jamie: I collected a flame trace from the node that closed the conn — shows write loop polling and then hitting abort path after 3 failed write attempts. I'll attach in the ticket.

eng-sre-bot: /notify eng-sre oncall -- severity: P2 potential customer outage (streaming disconnects + billing impact).

alex: Next steps for eng: can we change our slow-consumer abort to exponential backoff with streaming keepalive pings before hard close? That would reduce reconnect storms and duplicate billing. Also add metric for per-connection queued_bytes to surface before abort.

sasha: I'll take the Envoy config angle with the customer — ask them to try `per_connection_buffer_limit_bytes: 32768` and set `stream_idle_timeout` higher. Also ask them to enable TCP keepalives on the client.

maria: I'll prototype server-side mitigations: lower chunk size to 4KB, attempt async write queuing instead of immediate abort on first EAGAIN, and emit a diagnostic header `X-Redwood-Stream-Notice: slow-consumer` so clients can log and backoff.

jamie: Customer asked for short-term workaround. I told them: (1) add jitter to reconnects, (2) increase Envoy per-connection buffer and disable aggressive upstream aborts, (3) client should read with larger chunk_size to avoid small-window stalls. They want ETA.

alex: Rough ETA: config guidance to customer today. Quick server change (diagnostic header + metric) within 48 hrs. Deeper behavioral change (exponential backoff + queuing) needs spec + rollout 2-3 weeks.

sasha: +1, I'll send a customer-facing note summarizing repro, temporary config, and our plan. :thumbsup:

jamie: Thanks all — adding ticket link and logs in the support ticket. I'll follow up after we validate Envoy change with the customer.
